source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-62550:Worldborder not correctly initialized for the End and Nether
source_meta._title: Every dimension's world border is operating independently, and doesn't appear where it actually is

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition in a single-player world using the integrated server. Run the first listed affected version, Minecraft 1.12.2. Start in Creative mode with cheats/commands enabled. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: Select the Minecraft: Java Edition 1.12.2 installation in the launcher. Do not use the listed fix version, 1.18 Pre-release 1.
Use a new disposable world so that no earlier world-border settings, portals, beds, or spawn points affect the procedure.
Create the world in Creative mode with Allow Cheats enabled so that /worldborder, /tp, /fill, /spawnpoint, /kill, and /gamemode can be executed from in-game chat.
Use a single player for the reproduction. A dedicated server and additional players are not required by the report.
Keep the F3 debug screen available for verifying the current X, Y, and Z coordinates and facing direction.
The report supplies no world seed. The plan therefore constructs safe test areas at the exact command coordinates to remove terrain, lava, and hostile-mob interference.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft: Java Edition 1.12.2. From the main menu select Singleplayer, select Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has loaded into a new world in Creative mode and the hotbar is visible.

steps.action: Wait until the Overworld terrain surrounding the player has rendered and movement responds normally. Press F3 and confirm that coordinate information is visible.
steps.success_cue: The Overworld is responsive and the debug overlay displays X, Y, and Z coordinates.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the following command with the leading slash and press Enter. This moves the player to X=0, Y=100, Z=0, where the portal and respawn platform will be constructed.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Creative mode at approximately X=0, Y=100, Z=0.

steps.action: Press T, enter the following command with the leading slash, and press Enter. This creates an 11-by-11 cobblestone platform one block beneath the player.
steps.success_cue: A solid cobblestone platform exists from X=-5 through 5 and Z=-5 through 5 at Y=99.

steps.action: Set a deterministic personal respawn point at the center of the platform. Press T, enter the command with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the player's spawn point has been set at or near X=0, Y=100, Z=0.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to find Obsidian and Flint and Steel, then place both items in hotbar slots. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen; click or press the corresponding number key to make a slot active.
steps.exact_input: E; search for "Obsidian" and "Flint and Steel"
steps.success_cue: Obsidian and Flint and Steel are both available in the player's hotbar.

steps.action: On the platform, construct a Nether portal frame in the vertical plane Z=0. Place the four bottom obsidian blocks at X=2 through X=5, Y=100; four top blocks at X=2 through X=5, Y=104; and three side blocks at Y=101 through Y=103 on each of X=2 and X=5. Leave the six interior positions at X=3 through X=4, Y=101 through Y=103 empty.
steps.exact_input: Select Obsidian; right-click to place blocks at the specified coordinates
steps.success_cue: A complete 4-block-wide by 5-block-tall obsidian rectangle stands on the platform, with a 2-by-3 empty interior.

steps.action: Select Flint and Steel in the active hotbar slot. Aim at the top surface of either bottom interior obsidian block and right-click to ignite the portal interior.
steps.success_cue: The 2-by-3 interior of the obsidian frame is filled with the animated purple Nether-portal field.

steps.action: While still in the Overworld, press T to open chat. Enter the report's command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and chat confirms that the world-border diameter has been set to 1000 blocks.

steps.action: Walk into the purple portal field and remain inside it until dimension transfer begins. Do not issue another command while the portal transition is in progress.
steps.success_cue: The loading transition begins after the player remains inside the active portal.

steps.action: Wait until Nether terrain has rendered and player movement and chat commands respond normally. Do not continue while a loading screen is present or nearby chunks are still appearing.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Nether beside a generated return portal, surrounding chunks are rendered, and controls respond normally.

steps.action: Before shrinking the Nether border, prepare a safe test corridor at its intended center. Press T, enter the report's center teleport command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Nether at approximately X=0, Y=50, Z=0; Creative mode prevents terrain or lava at the destination from immediately harming the player.

steps.action: Wait until the chunks around X=0, Z=0 have loaded. Press F3 if needed and verify the displayed coordinates before constructing the corridor.
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay shows approximately X=0, Y=50, Z=0 and the local chunk is loaded.

steps.action: Construct the solid outer shell of an enclosed test corridor. Press T, enter the following command with the leading slash, and press Enter. The player may briefly be enclosed in blocks but cannot suffocate while in Creative mode.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that blocks were filled in the specified region.

steps.action: Hollow out the corridor immediately. Press T, enter the following command with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player stands in an enclosed, empty three-block-wide and three-block-high cobblestone corridor extending from approximately Z=-1 through Z=9, with a solid floor and no exposed lava.

steps.action: Return to the report's first Nether test position. Press T, enter the supplied command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Nether at approximately X=0, Y=50, Z=500.

steps.action: Wait until the destination chunk has rendered and chat commands respond. Remain in Creative mode even if the destination is inside terrain or lava.
steps.success_cue: The Nether chunk around X=0, Z=500 is loaded and the player can issue commands.

steps.action: While in the Nether, press T and execute the report's border-size command exactly, including the leading slash.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and chat confirms that the current dimension's world-border diameter has been set to 10 blocks.

steps.action: Press T and execute the report's query command exactly, including the leading slash. Record the displayed diameter without yet evaluating border rendering or player interaction.
steps.success_cue: The command completes successfully and a world-border diameter is displayed in chat for the Nether.

steps.action: Use a deliberate command death to return to the deterministic Overworld respawn platform without making border-induced death a prerequisite for continuing the setup. Press T, enter the command with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The death screen appears as a direct result of the /kill command and offers the Respawn button.

steps.action: Select Respawn and wait until the Overworld platform and nearby Nether portal have loaded.
steps.success_cue: The player has respawned in the Overworld near X=0, Y=100, Z=0, and the constructed portal is visible nearby.

steps.action: Ensure the player is in Creative mode before continuing. Press T, enter the command with the leading slash, and press Enter. The named Java game-mode command form was externally checked for historical use. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACommand_blocks_and_functions?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Creative flight and the Creative hotbar/inventory are available, and the player has no Survival health or hunger requirement for setup.

steps.action: While in the Overworld, execute the report's world-border query. Press T, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Preserve the displayed value for the observation subsystem without interpreting it during setup.
steps.success_cue: The command executes successfully in the Overworld and displays a border diameter in chat.

steps.action: Walk back into the nearby purple Nether portal field and remain inside it until dimension transfer begins.
steps.success_cue: The portal loading transition begins.

steps.action: Wait until the Nether and its return portal have fully loaded. Do not continue until movement and chat commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the Nether in Creative mode and the surrounding chunks are stable.

steps.action: Press T and execute the report's center teleport command exactly, including the leading slash.
steps.success_cue: The player is at approximately X=0, Y=50, Z=0 inside or immediately beside the previously constructed test corridor.

steps.action: Wait for the center chunk to finish loading. If the player is not already within the hollow corridor because of a fractional teleport position, move less than one block into its open interior. Verify with F3 that the position is close to X=0, Y=50, Z=0.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the clear corridor near X=0, Y=50, Z=0, with an unobstructed path toward increasing Z.

steps.action: Query the Nether border once more before changing game mode. Press T, enter the report's command with the leading slash, and press Enter. Record the displayed value without evaluating the bug.
steps.success_cue: The query succeeds in the Nether and displays the current border diameter in chat.

steps.action: Change to Survival mode while still near the center of the corridor. Press T, enter the command with the leading slash, and press Enter. The named Java game-mode command form was externally checked for historical use. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACommand_blocks_and_functions?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The Survival health and hunger bars are visible, and the player remains near X=0, Y=50, Z=0 inside the corridor.

steps.action: Open the F3 debug overlay and rotate the view until its facing line says south, toward positive Z. Do not move beyond approximately Z=1 during orientation.
steps.exact_input: F3; move the mouse until facing south/toward positive Z
steps.success_cue: The player is in Survival mode near Z=0 and is facing down the clear corridor toward increasing Z.

steps.action: Begin walking forward along the corridor toward increasing Z. Continue holding the move-forward control as the displayed Z coordinate approaches and attempts to pass Z=5 to Z=6. Do not jump, sprint, leave the corridor, or release the input before handing off.
steps.success_cue: Forward movement input is actively being held while the player attempts to traverse the corridor beyond the positive-Z edge of a 10-block-wide border centered at Z=0.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in Survival mode in the Nether, the Nether border was set to a diameter of 10, the Overworld border was previously set to 1000, and the player has just begun holding W toward positive Z through the prepared corridor while attempting to pass Z=5 to Z=6. Hand control to the observation subsystem now to inspect movement, position, damage state, and border rendering without performing additional setup actions.
uncertainties: The report supplies no world seed, so the exact Nether terrain at the two teleport destinations is unknown. The constructed center corridor removes terrain and lava as confounding factors for the final movement trigger.
Single-player was selected as the simplest deterministic environment. The report does not state that a dedicated server or multiple players are required.

The /kill command is an execution aid, not a condition stated by the report. It replaces waiting for border-induced death so that the reproduction plan does not depend on an observed bug outcome as a readiness condition.

The report also describes repeating the experiment in the End, using a border size other than 10, and repeating it with /worldborder center changes. Those are corroborating variants; this plan selects the shorter Nether size variant that establishes different per-dimension border settings and ends at the report's invisible-border movement trigger.
No fix-version reproduction is attempted. The listed fix version, 1.18 Pre-release 1, is intentionally excluded from recommended_version.
External verification was limited to historical Java game-mode command handling; all report-supplied /worldborder and /tp commands were preserved exactly.
